set.body:
VERIFIED. compile_frame(regions(labels), domain) accepts NA labels, silently excludes those features from every region, and silently rescales the regions that lose members. No warning, no diagnostic, and the returned frame looks structurally correct.

MEASURED, on a 4-feature domain with local normalization:

  labels                  rows   feature mass per column   features dropped
  r1,r1,r2,r2               2      0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5             0
  r1,r1,NA,r2               2      0.5, 0.5, 0,   1               1
  r1,NA,NA,r2               2      1,   0,   0,   1               2
  NA,NA,NA,NA             ERROR

Two distinct consequences, and the second is the one that changes numbers:

1. SILENT EXCLUSION. The NA feature contributes to nothing. Column mass 0. The frame still reports the expected number of regions, so nothing in the returned object says data was discarded.

2. SILENT RESCALING. Region r2 originally averaged features 3 and 4 at 0.5 each. With feature 3 NA-labelled, r2 becomes feature 4 alone at weight 1. So r2's value is now a DIFFERENT ESTIMAND - the mean of one voxel rather than two - and the user is not told their region shrank. In the two-NA case r1 shrinks the same way.

WHY THIS MATTERS IN REAL USE. Atlas and ROI label vectors routinely carry NA or 0 for unlabelled voxels; that is the normal shape of the data this argument exists to accept. A user handing effectagram a standard atlas vector gets a frame that silently omits every unlabelled voxel and rescales every partially-labelled region. The analysis runs, the output is well formed, and the regions are not the regions the user believes they specified.

IS THE BEHAVIOUR WRONG? Treating NA as 'belongs to no region' is a defensible SEMANTICS - arguably the right one. What is wrong is that it is silent, in a package whose entire stated position is that nothing about identity or membership should be inferred without an explicit declaration. Everywhere else this package refuses to guess: it will not accept a matching name and dimension as evidence of identity, it forces partition independence to be asserted, it rejects non-finite response data outright with 'Matrix response sources must be finite and nonempty'. Non-finite DATA is refused; non-finite LABELS are silently honoured. Those two policies are inconsistent.

FIX, in order of preference:
  1. document the NA policy on ?regions, and emit a message naming how many features were
     excluded and which regions were rescaled
  2. or require an explicit opt-in, e.g. regions(labels, unlabelled = 'drop'), so the
     exclusion is a declaration rather than a default
  3. at minimum, record the dropped count in the frame so a downstream receipt can carry it

NOTE ON SCOPE: I tested only regions(). The same question applies to any labelled spatial specification and to neuroim2_searchlights() with a mask containing NA, which I have not checked.
set.title: regions() silently drops NA-labelled features and rescales the surviving regions
